final:
`IntervalArray` now rejects an unsupported right-side dtype in the same way it rejects an unsupported left-side one. I haven't run or tested it, since I can't build anything here.

The fix is in `_ensure_simple_new_inputs` in `pandas/core/arrays/interval.py`. The category/object/string check only looked at `left.dtype`. It now checks `right.dtype` too. `pd.arrays.IntervalArray([pd.Interval(0, 2**64)])` should therefore raise the same `TypeError` as the mirrored case with `-(2**64)` on the left. I'd expect `pd.IntervalIndex` to behave the same, since I believe it builds through the same path, but I didn't check.

I chose the "raise the same `TypeError`" option from the issue rather than deriving the subtype from both endpoints. I didn't add a test.
